title: A separated group space is a scheme after algebraic closure
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] with algebraic closure $\overline{k}$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Let $G$ be a group algebraic space over $\operatorname{Spec}k$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]: its multiplication, identity and inverse are morphisms of sheaves satisfying the group identities on every test scheme. Assume $G$ is separated, meaning that $\Delta_{G/k}:G\to G\times_kG$ is representable by closed immersions [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Then the sheaf fibre product $G_{\overline{k}}=G\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}\overline{k}$ is represented by a $\overline{k}$-scheme. Fibre products of algebraic spaces use [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Fibre products of sheaves are computed on each test scheme and agree with [def-pc-fibre-product] for representable sheaves. No finite-type hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: The closed-immersion description on affine scheme tests shows that the diagonal of $G/k$ is quasi-compact: the inverse image of an affine test is $\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$. Thus $G$ satisfies the quasi-separated hypothesis needed below. For any extension $K/k$, $G_K$ is an algebraic space and its group operations are obtained by applying the operations of $G$ to the first coordinates of compatible pairs of sections. All group identities hold on test schemes. Apply the monic-diagonal test lemma with $Y=X_B=G_K$ and $j=1$: every scheme test of its diagonal is a test of the diagonal of $G/k$. Hence $G_K$ is separated and has quasi-compact diagonal as well.

proof.text: Choose a representable surjective etale scheme atlas $p:U\to G$ from the definition of algebraic space. Apply the large-field Jacobson lemma to this $U$ and choose its algebraically closed extension $K/k$. The base-changed atlas $p_K:U_K\to H=G_K$ remains surjective etale. In particular $U_K$ has closed points dense in every closed subset, and every closed point has residue field $K$. No finite-type assertion about $U$ is used.

proof.text: Let $W=H^{\mathrm{sch}}$ be the largest schematic open subspace furnished by the schematic-locus lemma. By Step 1 the diagonal $H\to H\times_KH$ is quasi-compact on scheme tests, so the dense-open-scheme lemma with $S=\operatorname{Spec}K$ and $Y=H$ gives a scheme $V_0$ and an open immersion $j:V_0\to H$ with $|V_0|$ open and dense in $|H|$. The image of $j$ is an open subspace represented by the scheme $V_0$, so maximality gives $j(V_0)\subseteq W$ and $|W|$ is dense in $|H|$. The identity section gives a point of $H$, so $|H|\neq\varnothing$ and the dense subset $|W|$ is nonempty. By the open-subspace/point correspondence and surjectivity of $p_K$, the inverse image $V=p_K^{-1}(W)$ is a nonempty open subscheme of $U_K$. The closed points are dense in $U_K$ (take the closed subset to be all of $U_K$), so $V$ contains a closed point $u$. Its residue field is $K$ by Step 2. Its residue-field morphism therefore gives a $K$-point $g^\prime$ of $W$.

proof.text: Every automorphism $a:H\to H$ preserves $W$. Indeed $a(W)\to H$ is an open subspace represented by the scheme $W$, so maximality gives $a(W)\subseteq W$. Apply the same argument to $a^{-1}$ and then apply $a$ to obtain the reverse inclusion. For any $g\in H(K)$ the natural map on test-scheme sections $h\mapsto g(g^\prime)^{-1}h$ is an automorphism, with inverse $h\mapsto g^\prime g^{-1}h$, by the group identities. It sends $g^\prime$ to $g$. Consequently every $K$-point of $H$ factors through $W$.

source.place: Tag 0B8E (lemma-group-space-scheme-over-kbar), translation automorphism and invariance of the largest schematic open

proof.text: The inverse image $V=p_K^{-1}(W)$ is all of $U_K$. To see this, its complement $C$ is closed in $U_K$. Every closed point $u$ of $U_K$ gives a $K$-point of $H$ by Step 2, hence maps into $W$ by Step 4 and belongs to $V$. Thus $C$ contains no closed point of $U_K$. The density clause of the large-field lemma applied to $Z=C$ says $C$ is the closure of the empty set, so $C=\varnothing$. Since $p_K$ is surjective on point classes, $|W|=|H|$. The open-subspace/point correspondence then gives $W=H$, and therefore $G_K$ is a scheme.

proof.text: Apply the field-extension schemeness lemma to $X=G$ and to the extension $K/k$ of Step 2. Its quasi-separated hypothesis was verified in Step 1 and $G_K$ is a scheme by Step 5. It follows that $G_{\overline{k}}$ is represented by a scheme, as claimed.
